note: Thu 12 Nov 2026 07:02 SGT run, against Wed 11 Nov US close. CNN Fear & Greed ticked up to 37 (Fear) from 33 the prior session -- a scraped secondary source mislabeled the overall rating 'Extreme Greed,' which is inconsistent with both the 0-100 banding and the component mix (3 Extreme Fear + 4 Neutral, no Greed), so it was corrected to 'Fear.' Despite Wed's sharp risk-on/vol-crush session (VIX -10.1% to 17.49), the Market Volatility component reads only Neutral, not yet Greed -- 17.49 is roughly in line with its recent trailing average rather than unusually low, and Put/Call plus Safe-Haven Demand are still deep in Extreme Fear from the preceding multi-week AI-led drawdown, so the composite has not flipped on a one-day bounce. Breadth looks broad on short/medium-term gauges (69% of S&P names above the 50-DMA, 1.48:1 advancers, a positive McClellan Summation Index) but narrower on a longer horizon -- only ~55-58% of names/sectors clear their 200-DMA and the Nasdaq racked up far more new lows (125) than new highs (65) even as the S&P made fresh highs. Flows are from the week ended 4 Nov 2026 (Lipper) with EM/Japan figures one reporting week further behind (week ended ~28 Oct) where no fresher region-specific breakout was found -- flagged per-region rather than blended silently.

flows.narrative: The most recent complete weekly tally (week ended Wed 4 Nov 2026) showed a seventh straight week of global equity inflows (+$38.6B, led by the US and a resurgent Europe) alongside the biggest weekly money-market inflow since April 2020 (+$172.7B) -- a barbell of continued risk-taking plus defensive cash-parking after the early-November AI-led growth-stock selloff. China equities extended a 10-week, ~$21B cumulative inflow streak even as China bonds kept bleeding, while gold ETFs logged their first net monthly inflow since July as the post-selloff safe-haven bid moderated into early November.
